interventions.speaker: CHAIR
interventions.who: the senior urologist who signs the decision
interventions.body:
The prognosis is influenced by several factors, including a preoperative PSA of 12.3 and the surgical finding of positive margins. The pathological grade was Gleason 3+4 (ISUP group 2), which contrasts with the biopsy findings showing initial grades of 3+3 and later 3+4. There were no documented seminal vesicle invasions or lymph nodes removed, meaning nodal status is unknown, widening uncertainty in risk assessment.

The absence of recorded postoperative PSA levels prevents any assessment of early biochemical recurrence trends. Future prognosis revision would critically depend on subsequent PSA measurements and their trajectory following surgery. The current data lacks information regarding the patient's follow-up history. The fixed estimated horizon is 56.82 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 34.09–79.54 months; its coverage has not been validated.
